patch.value: Session-topic provenance has no descriptor keys on any harness, and effort/role are wired for only claude-code and codex, so most fleet history records harness and model but nothing about the work's shape

The extensible provenance schema (ADR pm-oskdmu, shipped via pm-itsjf0) supports arbitrary dimensions, but the built-in descriptor table in src/core/shared/author.ts declares effort only for claude-code (CLAUDE_EFFORT) and codex (CODEX_REASONING_EFFORT/CODEX_EFFORT), role only for codex (CODEX_SESSION_ROLE), and topic for none of the seven agent harnesses (claude-code, codex, pi, opencode, cursor, aider, gemini-cli). Maintainers explicitly want attribution that includes the session topic and thinking level without any agent typing an identity flag. Each harness that exposes a topic/subject or effort signal needs its env keys declared; harnesses that expose none get an explicit null-mapping note so the gap is a documented harness limitation rather than an undiscovered omission.

Every built-in agent descriptor either declares keys for topic, effort and role or carries a recorded no-signal note for the missing dimension; detection tests prove each declared key flows into history provenance; fleet attribution (pm-gw6uyq) can group recorded history by topic and effort for the harnesses that expose them; no agent is ever required to set PM_AUTHOR or an identity flag
Attribution rich enough that per-harness, per-model, per-effort and per-topic fleet analytics (pm-gw6uyq) run on recorded history alone

Maintainer directive: harness, model, thinking level and session topic must all be auto-detected; the schema shipped extensible but the built-in descriptor table only covers two harnesses for effort and one for role

author: harness:claude-code
message: Backfill estimate for session-topic and effort/role provenance coverage

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Re-measured 2026-07-28 over 40,353 entries: zero carry any session topic, session role, or task-shape descriptor. Searching every entry key across the corpus, the complete set is ts, author, op, patch, before_hash, after_hash, message, author_source, agent_harness, agent_instance, agent_provenance and context. There is no session_topic, no agent_role, and no session key of any kind.

What this item can now treat as settled rather than open:

- The effort dimension SHIPPED and works. agent_provenance.effort reads {value: "xhigh", source: "environment"} on this session's entries, resolved from CLAUDE_EFFORT. So the claim that effort is wired for only two harnesses should be re-checked against the new agent_provenance shape rather than the old three-key descriptor, and the schema-extensibility objection is answered - a fourth dimension was added and populates.
- Sub-agent lineage signals ARE present in the environment and unused: CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID and CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1 are both set alongside CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, so a parent-child agent relationship is observable today and is recorded nowhere.
- Session TOPIC and ROLE remain the genuinely hard half, and the environment confirms why: nothing in the harness environment describes what the session is FOR. The full claude-code key set is CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_EFFORT, CLAUDE_PID. Topic and role are therefore not detectable in principle from this signal source and must be SUPPLIED, which is consistent with the disposition already recorded elsewhere that role has no signal source anywhere.

The useful reframing for this item: three of the four dimensions it asks for split cleanly by source. Harness and instance and effort are DETECTED and now work. Model is absent from the environment entirely and needs a non-environment source. Topic and role are semantic and can only be supplied by the caller or inferred from the work itself, for example from the items an agent touches during a session, which is the one option that keeps the automatic-identity mandate intact.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Evidence for the dimension coverage this item asks for, taken from the corpus rather than from the descriptors, 2026-07-29. Of 41,021 history entries, 1,475 carry an agent_provenance object, effort is present on 224 of those, and model is null on 1,475 of 1,475. agent_harness is null on 34,210 entries and populated on 6,811, split claude-code 4,525, codex 2,131, opencode 155. Separately, the 477 distinct author spellings in the same record decompose into precisely the dimensions this item is trying to add: codex-gpt5 encodes a model, codex-audit and codex-release-agent encode a role, codex-sdk-cli-consolidation-20260616 encodes a topic and a date. Writers were already recording topic, role and model - they had one free-text string to do it in. That is a stronger argument for declaring the dimensions than any descriptor gap, and it is worth citing in the item body. Vocabulary owner is pm-3yxwv5, read projection owner is pm-v8gfi7.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Live provenance census 2026-07-29: all 41,391 history events were inspected. Harness attribution exists on 7,181 recent events and effort exists on 307, but the activity schema exposes no usable session-topic population and model is null corpus-wide. The required result is a privacy-bounded, extensible descriptor contract with per-harness adapters and compact filtering/projection, not more free-text author spellings.
